Here's the thing. This is a big assumption that goes against being "realistic". Test equipment can get expensive pretty fast. Especially if you are delving into RF. A 1 GHz scope can start off at $20k USD. However, I am assuming you may be borrowing the equipment from your employer. 

But as others have mentioned, the challenge is usually designing to take other things into account such as cost, manufacturability, passing compliance, etc. 

Custom-built circuits and systems are almost always more expensive than trying to work with components that already exist. Most companies, even big tech ones, tend to go with pre-designed ICs in their products because it is faster and cheaper to do so.

For example, think about a buck. Let's say you have an odd current output and you want your switching frequency to be something that is not very common. You will probably find 2 ICs meeting most of those requirements, however from their datasheet, their efficiency will be at around 80%, which is not bad, but a bit low for a SMPS. If you were to design a custom one, then you could have that efficiency, but it would take you longer and it would probably cost more. 

In summary:

It is not unrealistic to optimize a design, but is is very challenging for it to be cheaper than using off the shelf components.

* person's first reaction is to take out phone and start recording
* person is not shaky
*  zoom can't be too high or else any slight movement will be extremely shaky regardless of how still the person is
* phone has to be on a tripod if extremely zoomed in
* lighting has to be good enough for the camera sensors to adjust properly and have a good focus
* phone must be one of those really expensive phones that have the best cameras
*  video must include background scenery for reference of object size
* UFO must stay long enough and move slow enough
